Define MCP tool schemas

Source: R/tool.R
tool-types.Rd

These helpers create common JSON Schema descriptions for tool arguments and output. type_from_schema() wraps a complete schema supplied as a list or JSON string without removing JSON Schema 2020-12 keywords. A complete tool input schema can be passed directly as arguments = type_from_schema(...) when it has direct root type = "object".

Usage

type_boolean(description = NULL, required = TRUE)

type_integer(description = NULL, required = TRUE)

type_number(description = NULL, required = TRUE)

type_string(description = NULL, required = TRUE)

type_enum(values, description = NULL, required = TRUE)

type_array(items, description = NULL, required = TRUE)

type_object(
  .description = NULL,
  ...,
  .required = TRUE,
  .additional_properties = FALSE
)

type_from_schema(text = NULL, path = NULL)

type_ignore()

Arguments

description

Optional argument description.

required

Whether the argument is listed as required in the parent schema. FALSE permits omission but does not set an R default.

values

Allowed enum values.

items

Type helper describing each array item.

.description

Optional object description.

...

Named properties for object schemas.

.required

Whether the object itself is listed as required in its parent schema.

.additional_properties

Whether to allow additional properties.

text

A JSON Schema as a list or JSON string.

path

Path to a JSON Schema file. Exactly one of text or path must be supplied.

Value

A lightweight mcplite tool type object.

Details

When $schema is absent, MCP treats schemas as JSON Schema 2020-12. Authors are responsible for schema validity and for runtime input/output conformance, domain validation, authorization or access checks, side-effect safety, output sanitization, and rate limiting where needed. List input preserves the supplied R list shape: use a named empty list for {} and an unnamed empty list for [].

Incoming JSON arrays remain R lists. These helpers do not coerce or validate argument values or supply R defaults. If an argument may be omitted, give the R function a default for it.

type_ignore() omits an argument from the advertised schema. It does not reject a caller-supplied argument or enforce permissions.

Examples

type_string("A label.")
#> $kind
#> [1] "string"
#> 
#> $description
#> [1] "A label."
#> 
#> $required
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "mcplite_tool_type_string" "mcplite_tool_type"       

type_array(type_integer(), description = "Integer values.")
#> $kind
#> [1] "array"
#> 
#> $description
#> [1] "Integer values."
#> 
#> $required
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $items
#> $kind
#> [1] "integer"
#> 
#> $description
#> NULL
#> 
#> $required
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "mcplite_tool_type_integer" "mcplite_tool_type"        
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "mcplite_tool_type_array" "mcplite_tool_type"      

type_object(
  .description = "A labeled score.",
  label = type_string(),
  score = type_number(required = FALSE)
)
#> $kind
#> [1] "object"
#> 
#> $description
#> [1] "A labeled score."
#> 
#> $required
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $properties
#> $properties$label
#> $kind
#> [1] "string"
#> 
#> $description
#> NULL
#> 
#> $required
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "mcplite_tool_type_string" "mcplite_tool_type"       
#> 
#> $properties$score
#> $kind
#> [1] "number"
#> 
#> $description
#> NULL
#> 
#> $required
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "mcplite_tool_type_number" "mcplite_tool_type"       
#> 
#> 
#> $additional_properties
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "mcplite_tool_type_object" "mcplite_tool_type"       

type_from_schema(list(
  type = "string",
  minLength = 1
))
#> $kind
#> [1] "schema"
#> 
#> $description
#> NULL
#> 
#> $required
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $schema
#> $schema$type
#> [1] "string"
#> 
#> $schema$minLength
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "mcplite_tool_type_schema" "mcplite_tool_type"
